1: Paul tells Timothy to stop people teaching speculation and myths. The aim of instruction is love from a pure heart. Paul calls himself the foremost of sinners, shown mercy as an example of Christ's patience.
"Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners." Paul never forgot what he had been forgiven.
2: Prayers should be offered for all people, including rulers. God wants everyone to be saved, and there is one mediator between God and humanity, the man Christ Jesus. Paul gives directions for conduct at worship.
God's saving will reaches every person. All Christian prayer goes to the Father through Christ.
3: Paul lists the qualities needed in a bishop and in deacons: self-controlled, faithful, able to manage their own household, respected by outsiders. The Church is "the pillar and foundation of the truth".
Character matters for those in office. The Church is called the support of truth, not merely a gathering of like-minded people.
4: False teachers will forbid marriage and certain foods, though everything God created is good. Timothy is to train in godliness and not let anyone look down on his youth, but to set an example and not neglect the gift given by the laying on of hands.
Young people can lead by example. Ordination by the laying on of hands gives a real gift.
5: Treat older men as fathers and younger women as sisters. The Church should support widows who are truly alone, while families care for their own. Elders who lead well deserve honour, and accusations against them need witnesses.
Faith includes practical duty to one's family. The Church organises its charity with care.
6: Those who want to be rich fall into temptation. The love of money is a root of all kinds of evil. Timothy must fight the good fight of faith. The rich should be generous and put their hope in God.
We brought nothing into the world and take nothing out. Contentment is great gain.
